patterns.pattern: Name the document type before capturing any characters
patterns.trigger: A flow needs a national/fiscal identifier and the caller has not said which document they hold (DNI vs NIE vs pasaporte vs NIF de empresa). Specialises 'Batch-ask all missing slots in one sentence' (opening/verification) by making document_type a slot in its own right.
patterns.example: [ES] "Para localizar su expediente necesito un documento. ¿Me lo da del DNI, del NIE o del pasaporte?"
patterns.check: A document_type slot is set in state before any character of the number is stored; the validator actually run matches that type; no DNI mod-23 check is ever run against a string captured as a passport; if the caller volunteers the number first, document_type is inferred from the shape and echoed once ('el NIE, entonces'), not silently assumed.

patterns.pattern: Normalize before validating: expand, strip, pad, uppercase
patterns.trigger: Any identifier arrives as spoken text: grouped numerals ('treinta y cuatro'), 'doble'/'triple'/'double', English 'oh' for zero, or ASR-inserted separators ('12.345.678-Z', '612-345-678'). Parent: 'Spelling and digit read-back' (opening/verification).
patterns.example: [ES] Caller: "doce, treinta y cuatro, cincuenta y seis, setenta y ocho, zeta." -> internal: expand -> 12345678 -> pad to 8 -> uppercase letter -> canonical 12345678Z.
patterns.check: Normalisation runs in the fixed order expand_spoken_numerals -> expand_repeat_words -> strip non-alphanumerics -> uppercase -> left-pad to the type's length, and the length/checksum test runs on the OUTPUT of that pipeline, never on ASR token count; tool arguments contain no spaces, dots, hyphens or lowercase; numeral words are never stored; a group whose value exceeds 99 (e.g. 'seiscientos doce') contributes 3 digits and the 2-vs-3-digit ambiguity is resolved by the type's total-length constraint, not by guessing.

patterns.pattern: Letter-vs-digit resolved by position, scoped to the identifier type
patterns.trigger: ASR returns 'O'/'oh' where the grammar requires a digit, or 'uno'/'I' where a letter sits — before asking anything. Specialises 'Mishearing / ASR repair' (repair & interruptions).
patterns.example: [EN] Caller reads a NIE: "Y, oh one two three four five six, Y" — the 'oh' is in a digit position, so it normalises to 0 -> Y0123456Y (checksum-valid).
patterns.check: Position in the type's grammar decides letter-vs-digit before any clarifying question is asked; the substitution table is PER TYPE, never global — O->0 and I->1 apply to DNI/NIE control positions (the 23-letter table TRWAGMYFPDXBNJZSQVHLCKE omits I, Ñ, O and U) but MUST NOT be applied to a CIF, whose control alphabet JABCDEFGHI contains I and whose entity letters include U (UTE); the agent asks a clarifying question only if the checksum then fails.

patterns.pattern: DNI/NIE mod-23 validated in-token, and a pass replaces the confirmation turn
patterns.trigger: A complete DNI or NIE has been captured and a lookup or write tool is next. Interacts with 'Confirm parameters before write tools' (before-tool) and with the 'Re-asking known information' anti-pattern.
patterns.example: [Internal] 12345678 mod 23 = 14 -> TRWAGMYFPDXBNJZSQVHLCKE[14] = 'Z' -> matches. Agent proceeds: [ES] "Perfecto, ya le veo, Ana. Su última factura es de..." — with no 'was that 12345678Z?' turn.
patterns.check: No tool call carries a DNI whose letter != TRWAGMYFPDXBNJZSQVHLCKE[int(digits) % 23], nor a NIE failing the same test after X->0/Y->1/Z->2 substitution; when the checksum passes the assistant turn contains NO yes/no confirmation question about the identifier (the checksum is the implicit confirmation, per Google conversation-design guidance that explicit confirmation is reserved for high-cost/irreversible steps); scored as a failure if an extra confirmation turn appears on a passing checksum.

patterns.pattern: No write tool with an unvalidated identifier
patterns.trigger: A create/update/transfer/payment/cancel tool is about to be called with an identifier argument. Extends 'Confirm parameters before write tools' (before-tool) with a hard, type-specific gate.
patterns.example: [Internal] submit_claim(dni=...) is the next step but the mod-23 check has not run -> run it; it fails -> re-ask the control letter; do NOT call submit_claim.
patterns.check: For every write-tool call in the trace, each identifier argument of a checksummable type (DNI/NIE mod-23, NIF-empresa mod-10, IBAN mod-97, card Luhn) is preceded in the same trace by a passing check; each identifier of a non-checksummable type (passport, order/ticket/confirmation code, email, DOB, postal code) is preceded by an explicit caller confirmation turn; a write call with neither is a hard fail regardless of whether the mock tool accepts it.

patterns.pattern: Checksum failure re-asks one segment, on a bounded budget
patterns.trigger: A mod-23, mod-10, mod-97 or Luhn check fails, or a length check fails. Specialises 'Validation error -> re-ask only the bad field' (errors & denials) down to sub-field granularity.
patterns.example: [ES] "Los ocho números me cuadran, pero la letra no me sale. ¿Me repite solo la letra del final?"
patterns.check: The re-ask names exactly one segment (digits OR control character OR one 2-digit phone group OR one 4-char IBAN chunk), never the whole identifier; already-accepted segments are not re-elicited; the re-prompt on attempt 2 is SHORTER and rephrased, not a verbatim repeat; at most 3 attempts per slot, after which the agent offers an alternative identifier or a callback/transfer rather than looping; the failing-segment index is chosen by the validator's reason code (TOO_SHORT/TOO_LONG -> counting problem -> re-ask the group; range/pattern failure -> re-ask the leading group; checksum-only failure -> re-ask the control character).

patterns.pattern: Disambiguate a letter with open-ended '<letra> de <palabra>'
patterns.trigger: A control-letter or code-letter re-ask, or the heard letter falls in a Spanish confusable set (B/V — a full phonemic merger in Spanish, M/N, S/F, P/T, C/Z/S in seseo areas, G/J, D/T). Specialises 'Spelling and digit read-back' (opening/verification).
patterns.example: [ES] Agent: "¿Es be de vaca o uve de vaso?" / Caller: "zeta, de Zaragoza."
patterns.check: The agent accepts '<letter> de <ANY word>' as an open construction and takes the first letter of the word as authoritative — no fixed city lookup table, since callers improvise ('B de burro', 'Z de zapato'); the agent's own disambiguating words never collide (never 'V de Valencia' against 'B de Barcelona' / Palencia; never a B-word and a V-word in the same pair); for a DNI/NIE control letter the agent never offers I, Ñ, O or U as candidates because the table excludes them; in English the NATO alphabet is used instead and 'as in' is accepted the same way.

patterns.pattern: NIE prefix letter is a first-class slot; an 'X/Y/Z DNI' routes silently to the NIE validator
patterns.trigger: The caller is a foreign resident, the captured string is 7 digits + letter with no leading letter heard, or the caller says 'mi DNI es...' and the string begins with X, Y or Z.
patterns.example: [ES] "El NIE empieza por una letra: ¿es equis, i griega o zeta?" — and later, if the caller called it a DNI, the agent validates it as a NIE without saying 'eso no es un DNI'.
patterns.check: Canonical form matches ^[XYZ][0-9]{7}[A-Z]$; the checksum substitutes X->0, Y->1, Z->2 before the mod-23; the prefix is never defaulted to X and never inferred from nationality; the clarifying question enumerates the three options rather than being open-ended; document_type is silently reclassified to NIE with no pedantic correction turn (a correction turn is scored as a 'Re-asking known information'-class failure); the Y0123456Y shape (prefix letter and control letter both Y) is handled without dropping either Y.

patterns.pattern: NIF de empresa: entity letter cross-checked, control class checked before arithmetic
patterns.trigger: A 9-character company NIF/CIF is captured, or the caller has already said the legal form ('somos una ese ele', 'el ayuntamiento', 'la asociación').
patterns.example: [ES] "Al ser una ese ele, el NIF empieza por be, ¿verdad? Be, y luego los siete números."
patterns.check: The first character matches the Orden EHA/451/2008 key implied by the stated form (S.A.->A, S.L.->B, colectiva->C, comanditaria->D, comunidad de bienes->E, cooperativa->F, asociación->G, comunidad de propietarios->H, sociedad civil->J, corporación local->P, organismo público->Q, congregación religiosa->R, órgano de la Administración->S, UTE->U, otros->V, entidad extranjera->N, establecimiento permanente de no residente->W); the whitelist ALSO accepts the personal-NIF letters K (menores), L (españoles no residentes) and M (no residentes sin NIE), which come from RD 1065/2007 and not from that Order, so valid personal NIFs are never rejected; the control-character CLASS is checked before the arithmetic (P/Q/R/S/N/W must end in a letter; A/B/E/H must end in a digit; others either) and a class violation re-asks WHICH DOCUMENT the caller is reading rather than re-asking the digits, because Spanish has no digit-to-letter homophony that would produce a spurious trailing letter; on a class-consistent mod-10 mismatch the behaviour is the same hard gate as the DNI (targeted re-ask, never a tool call).

patterns.pattern: 'Número de soporte' is not the DNI number
patterns.trigger: A DNI was requested but the captured string has the 3-letters + 6-digits shape, or a DNI-shaped string fails mod-23 while a support-number-shaped string is also in the transcript.
patterns.example: [ES] "Creo que me ha leído el número de soporte. El del DNI está justo debajo de su foto: ocho números y una letra al final."
patterns.check: A 3-alpha + 6-numeric string captured under a DNI request is classified as a support-number mix-up, not reported to the caller as an invalid DNI; the repair turn names WHERE ON THE CARD to look instead of repeating the same question; the same handling applies to a TIE support number (E + 8 digits) and to a Certificado de Registro de Ciudadano de la UE (C + number left-padded with zeros to 8 digits); the agent never claims to distinguish a DNIe support number from a Spanish passport number by shape alone, because the two shapes are identical.

patterns.pattern: Passport: permissive shape, explicit read-back, never claim validation
patterns.trigger: The caller supplies a passport number (Spanish or foreign) and there is no published check algorithm the agent can run.
patterns.example: [ES] "Le repito el pasaporte: pe, a, be — y luego uno dos tres, cuatro cinco seis. ¿Es correcto?"
patterns.check: The shape gate is permissive (Spanish: 2-3 letters followed by 6 digits, 8 or 9 characters total; foreign: 6-9 alphanumerics, letters and digits mixed) and never a hard 3-alpha+6-numeric reject; because no algorithm is published, an EXPLICIT yes/no confirmation is required before the tool call — the opposite of the DNI rule; letters are read back individually with the spelling alphabet and digits in groups of three; the agent never says the number 'is valid' or 'checks out'; the MRZ check digit (ICAO 9303, weights 7-3-1 repeating, A=10..Z=35, '<'=0, mod 10) is used ONLY when the caller is already reading a scan or photo of the machine-readable lines, never as a live-voice instruction, because '<' fillers are unpronounceable; a passport number is never recognised from a previous call, since it changes on renewal.

patterns.pattern: Spanish phone number: exactly nine digits, no trunk zero, 3-2-2-2 read-back, range class gated
patterns.trigger: A Spanish phone number is captured, or a captured number is about to be used by an SMS/WhatsApp/callback tool.
patterns.example: [ES] "Le confirmo el móvil: seiscientos doce, treinta y cuatro, cincuenta y seis, setenta y ocho. ¿Le mando ahí el SMS?"
patterns.check: National number is exactly 9 digits matching (?:400|[5-9][0-9][0-9])[0-9]{6}; a leading 0 the caller or ASR produced is DELETED, never stored, because Spain has no national trunk prefix; read-back is chunked 3-2-2-2, except 800/900 numbers which are chunked 3-3-3; before any SMS/WhatsApp tool the agent gates on number_type == MOBILE (6xx, 71-74, 78) and NOT on the leading digit — 70x is a personal number, 51x a nomadic UAN, 80[367] premium, 90[12] shared cost, [89]00 toll-free — and a non-mobile is re-asked ('ese número no admite SMS, ¿tiene un móvil?') rather than silently sent to; the ITN layer's 3-3-3 grouping is stripped and re-chunked to 3-2-2-2 before speaking.

patterns.pattern: International number: region-aware normalization to E.164, extension as a separate slot
patterns.trigger: The caller says '+34', 'más treinta y cuatro', 'cero cero treinta y cuatro', '011', a foreign trunk zero, or an extension ('extensión', 'anexo', 'interno', 'ext', 'x').
patterns.example: [EN] Caller: "double oh three four, nine one five five five, twelve, thirty-four, extension one two three." -> phone=+34915551234, extension=123 — two fields, not one string.
patterns.check: The canonical tool argument is '+' + country code + national significant number, no separators, at most 15 digits (ITU-T E.164 §6.1, which excludes the international prefix from the count); international prefixes ('00', '011') and national trunk prefixes are treated as dialling instructions and deleted, NOT as data (E.164 §7.3.1-7.3.2); '00' is mapped to '+' only when the parsing region's IDD actually is 00, so the call's default region must be present in state and used — a US-region caller saying 'zero zero three four' is not silently read as +34; leading-zero handling is delegated to a libphonenumber-class library and never hand-written in the prompt (libphonenumber deliberately keeps a leading zero in regions with no national prefix, e.g. IT); the extension is stored in its own field and NEVER concatenated onto the E.164 string; a phone field whose digit count exceeds the region's possible length triggers the extension-vs-number question, not a truncation.

patterns.pattern: IBAN: four-character chunks, mod-97 before any payment tool
patterns.trigger: An IBAN or Spanish CCC is captured for a direct debit, refund or transfer.
patterns.example: [ES] "Vamos por partes: ES nueve uno... ahora los cuatro siguientes... " then read-back: "Termina en cinco uno tres tres dos, del banco 2100. ¿Confirmamos la domiciliación?"
patterns.check: Spanish IBAN is exactly 24 characters matching ^ES[0-9]{22}$ (SWIFT IBAN Registry format ES2!n4!n4!n1!n1!n10!n: 2 check digits, 4 bank, 4 branch, 2 national check digits, 10 account); mod-97 is computed over the whole string with the first four characters rotated to the end and letters mapped A=10..Z=35, and must equal 1; capture and read-back are in 4-character chunks so a failing chunk can be re-asked by index; the two Spanish national check digits are additionally verified with the CCC weights [1,2,4,8,5,10,9,7,3,6] over '00'+bank+branch and over the account (remainder 10->1, 11->0), which localises the error to the bank/branch half or the account half; a mod-97 failure never reaches a payment tool and never produces an 'invalid account' statement to the caller — it produces a chunk-level re-ask; the spoken read-back gives only the last four characters plus the bank name, never the full 24.

patterns.pattern: Card: last four and expiry only; a full PAN is refused, not repeated, not retained
patterns.trigger: The caller starts reading a full card number or a CVV, or the flow needs to identify which card an account holds.
patterns.example: [EN] Caller: "Sure, it's four one one one, four one one—" Agent: "Sorry to stop you — I only need the last four digits, never the whole number. What are the last four?"
patterns.check: The agent interrupts a full-PAN or CVV recitation at the earliest opportunity and states that it does not need it; no assistant turn ever contains more than the last 4 digits of a PAN; a CVV/CVC, full track data or PIN is never requested, never echoed and never placed in a tool argument, because PCI DSS forbids RETAINING sensitive authentication data after authorisation and a transcript, log or call recording is retention (this is the operative constraint for a voice agent — display masking is a separate, weaker requirement whose current v4.x ceiling is BIN + last four, not the superseded 'first six and last four'); card matching is done by last-4 + expiry month/year, with expiry read back as 'month/year' words not a slash; if the platform supports it, full card entry is routed to DTMF/secure-capture rather than to the agent's ASR; Luhn is applied only where a full PAN legitimately reaches the tool layer, never in the spoken channel.

patterns.pattern: Masked read-back of an identifier already on file
patterns.trigger: The agent must confirm or reference an identifier it already holds (from a tool result or earlier in the call) rather than one the caller is currently dictating.
patterns.example: [ES] "Confirmo: el documento acabado en cuatro cinco seis, letra ese, y la cuenta terminada en uno tres tres dos. ¿Todo correcto?"
patterns.check: Spoken output never contains a full DNI, NIE, passport, IBAN or PAN retrieved from a tool result; the mask is per type — DNI/NIE: last 3 digits + control letter; passport: last 3 characters; IBAN: last 4; card: last 4; phone: last 3 with the network class named ('el móvil que acaba en 678'); email: first character of the local part + domain; the UNMASKED value still goes to the tool; the mask is applied to the assistant's text, not to the state, so the agent can still match what the caller says against the full value; a masked read-back is scored as failing if the caller could not distinguish two records on file from it — in that case one extra distinguishing field is added rather than unmasking.

patterns.pattern: Ask only identifiers an in-scope tool signature requires
patterns.trigger: Start of a verification step, or the temptation to collect a 'just in case' second identifier. Interacts with 'Verify identity before any account data' (opening/verification) and the 'Re-asking known information' anti-pattern.
patterns.example: [ES] "Con su documento ya le localizo" — the postal code is asked only after the first lookup returns more than one match or a mismatch.
patterns.check: Every identifier the agent requests is a required (or, after a documented mismatch, an optional-disambiguating) argument of a tool that is actually in scope for this system prompt; requesting an identifier no in-scope tool consumes is a hard fail (data minimisation, GDPR art. 5.1.c — the AEPD has fined a business 2.000 EUR, reduced to 1.600 EUR, for collecting a phone number that its stated invoicing purpose did not require); the agent never asks the caller to send a photo or copy of a document; a stronger or additional identifier is escalated to only after a recorded mismatch or an ambiguous match, never pre-emptively; note this minimisation rule governs WHICH fields to ask for, and does not override a domain's own authentication requirements (e.g. payment flows), which the system prompt states separately.

patterns.pattern: Email spelled aloud: token the separators, shortlist the domain
patterns.trigger: The caller dictates an email address, in either language, using 'arroba'/'at', 'punto'/'dot', 'guion'/'dash', 'guion bajo'/'underscore', 'todo junto', 'en minúscula'.
patterns.example: [ES] Caller: "ana punto lópez arroba gmail punto com" -> ana.lopez@gmail.com. Agent: "¿Es gmail punto com, o gmail punto es?"
patterns.check: 'arroba'/'at' maps to @, 'punto'/'dot' to '.', 'guion'/'dash'/'hyphen' to '-', 'guion bajo'/'underscore' to '_'; accents and ñ dictated in the local part are folded to ASCII and the fold is confirmed once ('sin tilde, ¿verdad?'); the whole address is lowercased; the domain is confirmed against a shortlist of the common providers rather than spelled letter by letter when it matches one (gmail/hotmail/outlook/yahoo/icloud + the caller's stated employer domain), while an unrecognised domain IS spelled back; the local part is always spelled back character by character; the address must match a basic syntax check with exactly one @ and a dot-bearing domain before any send/subscribe tool; 'todo junto' suppresses separator insertion rather than being transcribed.

patterns.pattern: Date of birth and postal code: resolve the format, cross-check the context
patterns.trigger: A DOB or postal code is captured as a verification factor, especially in a bilingual call where day/month order differs by convention.
patterns.example: [EN] Caller: "Oh-five, oh-nine, sixty-two." Agent: "Just so I have it right — is that the fifth of September, or the ninth of May?"
patterns.check: An all-numeric date whose first two components are both <= 12 triggers ONE disambiguating question naming both readings in words; a 2-digit year is resolved by a stated century rule (a DOB year that would make the caller under 16 or over 110 flips the century) and never silently defaulted; the stored value is ISO yyyy-mm-dd in the tool argument while the spoken form stays natural ('cinco de septiembre del sesenta y dos') per 'Spoken formatting of dates, money, IDs' (result narration); a Spanish postal code is exactly 5 digits with the leading zero preserved ('cero ocho cero cero cuatro' -> 08004) and its first two digits (01-52, province) are cross-checked against any town or province the caller has already named — a mismatch is a targeted re-ask of the postal code, not of the address; DOB and postal code are non-checksummed, so both require an explicit confirmation before a write tool.

patterns.pattern: Alphanumeric confirmation code: clarify the confusable set, read back explicitly, invent no checksum
patterns.trigger: An order, ticket, booking, case or confirmation code mixing letters and digits is captured or returned. Extends 'Confirmation-number read-back after a write' (result narration) to the inbound direction.
patterns.example: [EN] Agent: "I have B-R-4-9-2-K. That's B as in bravo, R as in romeo, four nine two, K as in kilo — right?"
patterns.check: Codes are read back in chunks of 3-4 characters with a spelling alphabet on every letter; the agent proactively disambiguates the glyph-confusable set at the point of capture (0/O, 1/I/L, 5/S, 2/Z, 8/B, and in Spanish additionally B/V and M/N) instead of after a failed lookup; hyphens and slashes the caller omits or the ASR drops are re-inserted from the code's known template rather than being treated as data ('MBR-99021' must not become '99021'); case is normalised to the template's case; because no checksum exists, an explicit yes/no confirmation is required before a lookup or write; the agent never asserts a code is 'not a valid code' — it reports only that the lookup found nothing and offers a different handle (phone, email, date of purchase) after at most 2 failed attempts.

identifier_spec.format: 8 digits + 1 control letter, canonical `^[0-9]{8}[A-Z]$` (e.g. 12345678Z). Older documents with fewer printed digits are left-padded with zeros to 8.
identifier_spec.checksum: VERIFIED, computable offline: letter = "TRWAGMYFPDXBNJZSQVHLCKE"[int(digits) % 23]. Ministerio del Interior worked example: 12345678 -> resto 14 -> Z. Table is 23 letters and deliberately omits I, Ñ, O, U to avoid confusion with 1, l and 0. Reproduced locally: 00123456->S, 65432198->G, 00000000->T, 99999999->R.
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_en: "one two three four five six seven eight, zed" / "twelve thirty-four fifty-six seventy-eight, Z" / "...Z as in Zulu" / "double zero one two three four five six, S".
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_es: Habitualmente en pares: "doce, treinta y cuatro, cincuenta y seis, setenta y ocho, zeta". También "uno dos tres..." dígito a dígito, "doble cero", "triple siete", y la letra desambiguada con "zeta de Zaragoza", "ese de Sevilla". Algunos dicen "ocho millones..." para el número entero (raro pero ocurre).
identifier_spec.asr_confusions: Two-digit collapse (dieciséis/sesenta, sesenta/setenta, cuatro/cuarenta); dropped leading zeros; control letter B/V (single phoneme in Spanish), S/F, M/N, C/Z (seseo), G/J, D/T, P/B; 'zeta' heard as 'ese'; in EN, fifteen/fifty and 'oh' for 0. Letter/digit homophony cannot affect the control letter because I, O, U are excluded from the table.
identifier_spec.normalization: expand spoken numerals and doble/triple -> strip separators (dots, hyphens, spaces) -> uppercase -> left-pad digits to 8 -> validate mod 23. Store canonical 9-char string with no separator.
identifier_spec.readback_policy: When the checksum PASSES: no confirmation turn — proceed and fold the value into the next sentence. When re-asking or when referring to a DNI already on file: masked to last 3 digits + control letter ("acabado en cuatro cinco seis, letra ese"). Never speak all 8 digits back.

identifier_spec.format: Prefix X, Y or Z + 7 digits + 1 control letter, `^[XYZ][0-9]{7}[A-Z]$` (e.g. X1234567L, Y0123456Y, Z1234567R).
identifier_spec.checksum: VERIFIED: substitute X->0, Y->1, Z->2, prepend to the 7 digits, then the identical mod-23 table. Reproduced locally: X1234567->L, Y0123456->Y, Z1234567->R, Z0123456->C, X0000000->T.
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_en: "X, one two three four five six seven, L" / "ex-ray one two three..." / callers often call it "my DNI" or "my NIE number".
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_es: "equis, uno dos tres cuatro cinco seis siete, ele"; "i griega" or "ye" for Y; "zeta" for Z; frecuentemente el llamante dice "mi DNI" aunque sea NIE. La marca de prefijo a veces se omite del todo ("cero uno dos tres...").
identifier_spec.asr_confusions: Prefix dropped entirely (yielding 7 digits + letter, indistinguishable from a truncated DNI); 'i griega' vs 'ele'; Y0123456Y — prefix and control letter both Y, so one Y is easily lost; equis/ese; zeta/ese; same digit-group collapses as DNI.
identifier_spec.normalization: Same pipeline as DNI, plus: if the string is 7 digits + letter and no prefix was heard, ASK for the prefix (never default to X). Substitute prefix only inside the checksum computation; store the letter form.
identifier_spec.readback_policy: Same as DNI: silent on a pass; masked (last 3 + control letter) when referencing one on file. If a prefix re-ask is needed, enumerate the three options ('¿equis, i griega o zeta?') rather than asking openly.

identifier_spec.identifier: CIF / NIF de persona jurídica (and personal NIF K/L/M)
identifier_spec.format: 9 characters: entity letter + 7 digits + control character, `^[A-HJ-NP-SUVW][0-9]{7}[0-9A-J]$`. Entity letters per Orden EHA/451/2008: A S.A., B S.L., C colectivas, D comanditarias, E comunidades de bienes, F cooperativas, G asociaciones, H comunidades de propietarios, J sociedades civiles, P corporaciones locales, Q organismos públicos, R congregaciones religiosas, S órganos de la Administración, U UTEs, V otros, N entidades extranjeras, W establecimientos permanentes de no residentes. Personal NIFs K (menores), L (españoles no residentes), M (no residentes sin NIE) come from RD 1065/2007 and must also be accepted.
identifier_spec.checksum: HIGH confidence (algorithm not published in the BOE Order — Orden EHA/451/2008 says only 'c) Un carácter de control' — but validated locally against 11 real Spanish NIFs: A28015865, A39000013, A48010615, A78374725, A15075062, A82018474, A58818501, B84325752, B12345674, Q2826000H, G28029643, all matching). A = sum of the even-position digits (2nd,4th,6th of the 7); B = for each odd-position digit, double it and sum the digits of the product; E = (A+B) mod 10; D = (10-E) mod 10; control = str(D) or "JABCDEFGHI"[D]. Class rule (secondary source only): letter required for P,Q,R,S,N,W; digit required for A,B,E,H; either otherwise.
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_en: "A, twenty-eight, oh one five eight six five" / "B as in bravo, eight four three two five seven five two".
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_es: "a, veintiocho, cero quince, ochocientos sesenta y cinco"; "be de Barcelona, ocho cuatro tres dos..."; el llamante suele decir "el CIF" aunque legalmente sea el NIF; a veces antepone la forma jurídica ("somos una ese ele").
identifier_spec.asr_confusions: Entity letter B/V, A/H (in fast speech), G/J, Q/K, P/B, U/V (and 'U' of UTE lost); control letter I heard as 1 and J heard as 'jota'/'ge'; the seven digits collapse exactly like a DNI's. CRITICAL: do NOT apply the DNI's I/O/U-exclusion normalisation here — the control alphabet JABCDEFGHI contains I, and U is a valid entity letter.
identifier_spec.normalization: expand numerals -> strip separators -> uppercase -> assert 9 chars -> class check on the control character -> mod-10 arithmetic. Store as-is; never rewrite the entity letter.
identifier_spec.readback_policy: Cross-check the entity letter against the legal form the caller already stated, as a question rather than a correction ('al ser una ese ele empieza por be, ¿verdad?'). Company NIFs are business-register public data, so a full read-back is acceptable where a DNI's would not be; still prefer chunked (letter, then 3+4 digits). A control-class violation re-asks WHICH DOCUMENT is being read.

identifier_spec.format: UNVERIFIED-shape: currently issued numbers are widely described as 3 letters + 6 digits (9 characters), but no Policía Nacional or Ministerio del Interior page stating the format was found, and Microsoft Purview's Spain-passport definition accepts 8 OR 9 characters (2 alphanumerics + 1 optional + 6 digits). Use a PERMISSIVE gate: `^[A-Z]{2,3}[0-9]{6}$`. Shape collides exactly with the DNIe 'número de soporte' (3 letters + 6 digits).
identifier_spec.checksum: NONE the agent can run. Sources conflict on whether a control character exists and where: BBVA says a control character is added beyond the nine and is printed only on the authorities' page; Signe (which performs Spanish passport numbering) says the THIRD LETTER is itself a check digit. No algorithm is published either way. The only computable check is the ICAO Doc 9303 MRZ check digit (weights 7-3-1 repeating, digits 0-9, A=10..Z=35, '<'=0, mod 10) over the 9-character document-number field — usable only when the caller is reading a scan of the machine-readable lines.
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_en: "P-A-B, one two three, four five six" / "papa alpha bravo, one twenty-three, four fifty-six".
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_es: "pe, a, be — uno dos tres, cuatro cinco seis"; con desambiguación local: "pe de Palencia, a de Ávila, be de Barcelona".
identifier_spec.asr_confusions: All three letters are in confusable sets (B/V/P, M/N, S/F, C/Z, G/J); no checksum to catch a single-character error, so the read-back IS the only detection layer; the number changes on every renewal, so a value remembered from a previous call is stale by construction.
identifier_spec.normalization: strip separators -> uppercase -> permissive shape gate. Never left-pad. Never reclassify a 3+6 string as a DNI support number without asking.
identifier_spec.readback_policy: MANDATORY explicit yes/no read-back before any tool call — the opposite of the DNI rule. Letters individually with a spelling alphabet, digits in groups of three. Never state that the number 'is valid'. When referencing one on file: last 3 characters only.

identifier_spec.format: Heterogeneous. Practical gate: 6-9 alphanumerics, at least one digit, uppercase, no separators. Country is a separate slot (the issuing state, not the caller's nationality). Some LatAm passports are all-numeric; some EU ones are all-alphanumeric with letter prefixes.
identifier_spec.checksum: None generally available. ICAO 9303 MRZ 7-3-1 check digits exist on every machine-readable passport (document number, DOB, expiry, and a composite), but again only usable from a scan, not from live voice.
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_en: NATO alphabet is common among frequent travellers; otherwise 'B as in boy'. Digits usually one by one.
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_es: "be de burro", "ce de casa" — improvised words, not a fixed table. Los llamantes latinoamericanos suelen leer dígito a dígito, no en pares como en España.
identifier_spec.asr_confusions: Same glyph-confusable set as confirmation codes (0/O, 1/I/L, 5/S, 2/Z, 8/B); code-switching mid-string (a Spanish speaker reading letters with English names, or vice versa) is common and must be accepted.
identifier_spec.normalization: strip separators -> uppercase -> shape gate -> store with the issuing-country slot. Never assume Spanish shape.
identifier_spec.readback_policy: Explicit read-back, chunked 3-4 characters, spelling alphabet on every letter. Ask for the issuing country BEFORE the number so the shape gate can be selected.

identifier_spec.format: Exactly 9 digits, `(?:400|[5-9][0-9][0-9])[0-9]{6}`. NO national trunk prefix exists in Spain. Written/spoken grouping 3-2-2-2, except 800/900 which group 3-3-3. Ranges: 6xx and 71/72/73/74/78 mobile; 70x PERSONAL NUMBER (not mobile); 51x nomadic/UAN; 8xx and 9xx geographic; 80[367] premium; 90[12] shared cost; [89]00 toll-free.
identifier_spec.checksum: None. The available programmatic checks are length (exactly 9), the leading-digit pattern, and libphonenumber's isValidNumber + number_type.
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_en: "six one two, three four, five six, seven eight" / "six twelve, thirty-four, fifty-six, seventy-eight" / "oh oh three four" prefixed.
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_es: Pares es lo normal: "seiscientos doce, treinta y cuatro, cincuenta y seis, setenta y ocho". También "seis uno dos...", "doble cinco", "triple ocho", "más treinta y cuatro", "cero cero treinta y cuatro", "punto" usado como separador entre grupos.
identifier_spec.asr_confusions: Two-digit collapse is the dominant failure (cuarenta vs cuatro — 'cuarenta' contributes TWO digits; sesenta/setenta; dieciséis/sesenta); a spurious leading 0 from a foreign-style trunk habit; ITN layers regroup 9 digits as 3-3-3 which mismatches the caller's 3-2-2-2 mental model; 'punto' transcribed literally.
identifier_spec.normalization: expand numerals and doble/triple -> delete 'punto'/dots/hyphens/spaces -> delete a leading 0 for ES (Spain has no trunk prefix) -> assert exactly 9 digits -> classify by range -> store E.164 (+34 + the 9 digits).
identifier_spec.readback_policy: One read-back of the whole number, chunked 3-2-2-2 (or 3-3-3 for 800/900), never a yes/no after each group. Explicit confirmation IS warranted because the number is about to be written to the account or messaged. When referencing one on file: last 3 digits plus the class ('el móvil acabado en 678').

identifier_spec.format: E.164: '+' + country code (1-3 digits) + national significant number, at most 15 digits EXCLUDING the international prefix (ITU-T E.164 §6.1). Extension is a SEPARATE field (RFC 3966 ';ext='); practical cap 1-4 digits for ES, up to 6-20 elsewhere depending on how explicitly it was labelled.
identifier_spec.checksum: None. Two distinct programmatic gates: isPossibleNumber (length-only, returns TOO_SHORT / TOO_LONG / INVALID_COUNTRY_CODE / INVALID_LENGTH) and isValidNumber (length + prefix pattern). Neither means the line exists.
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_en: "plus three four...", "double oh three four...", "zero one one...", "...extension one two three", "...ext one twenty-three", "...x123".
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_es: "más treinta y cuatro", "cero cero treinta y cuatro", "...extensión ciento veintitrés", "...anexo", "...interno" (LatAm).
identifier_spec.asr_confusions: '00' vs '+' conflated (invalid outside regions whose IDD is 00 — in the US '00' is not an IDD); foreign trunk zeros (GB/FR/DE '0', AR '0' and '15') kept or stripped wrongly; Italy's leading 0 must be KEPT; extension digits silently appended to the number, producing a plausible-length but undialable string.
identifier_spec.normalization: Delegate to a libphonenumber-class library with the call's default region in state; never hand-write leading-zero rules in the prompt. Split the extension on 'ext/extensión/anexo/interno/x/#' BEFORE parsing. Store phone=E.164, extension=digits.
identifier_spec.readback_policy: Read back in the destination country's national grouping (what the caller will recognise) while the TOOL receives E.164. Read the extension as a separate clause ('...extensión uno dos tres'). Explicit confirmation required.

identifier_spec.format: Spain: 24 characters, `^ES[0-9]{22}$`. SWIFT IBAN Registry format ES2!n4!n4!n1!n1!n10!n = ES + 2 IBAN check digits + 4 bank + 4 branch + 2 national check digits + 10 account. The trailing 20 digits are the legacy CCC. Foreign IBANs: 2-letter country + 2 check digits + up to 30 BBAN characters (e.g. GB is 22).
identifier_spec.checksum: TWO, both verified locally. (1) ISO 13616 mod-97: move the first 4 characters to the end, map letters A=10..Z=35, interpret as an integer, remainder must be 1 (verified on ES9121000418450200051332, ES7921000813610123456789, GB82WEST12345698765432). (2) Spanish CCC national check digits: weights [1,2,4,8,5,10,9,7,3,6]; d1 over '00'+bank+branch, d2 over the 10-digit account; r = 11 - (sum mod 11), with 10->'1' and 11->'0'. Verified: bank 2100, branch 0418, account 0200051332 -> '45', exactly the DC pair in the ISO reference IBAN.
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_en: "E-S nine one, two one zero zero, oh four one eight..." — usually read in 4-character chunks from the card or app.
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_es: "e ese, noventa y uno, dos mil cien, cero cuatro dieciocho, cuarenta y cinco, cero dos cero cero cero cinco uno tres tres dos"; muchos leen de la app en bloques de cuatro; algunos dan sólo el CCC de veinte dígitos sin el ES.
identifier_spec.asr_confusions: 24 characters is far beyond a single-utterance reliable capture — errors accumulate; 'ES' heard as 'e ese'/'es'; two-digit collapse inside every chunk; chunk boundaries lost so the total drifts by one digit; a caller reading the legacy 20-digit CCC when an IBAN was asked for.
identifier_spec.normalization: strip spaces/hyphens -> uppercase -> if 20 digits and ES context, prepend ES and COMPUTE the two IBAN check digits rather than asking -> assert 24 chars -> mod-97 -> CCC DC check to localise a failure. Store with no separators.
identifier_spec.readback_policy: Capture and re-ask by 4-character chunk index. Read back only the last 4 characters plus the bank name ('termina en 1332, del 2100'). Never speak the full 24 characters. Explicit confirmation required before any payment/direct-debit tool, in addition to the mod-97 pass.

identifier_spec.identifier: Card: last four + expiry (full PAN never)
identifier_spec.format: Captured: last4 = `^[0-9]{4}$`; expiry = MM/YY with MM in 01-12 and the year within the next ~10. NOT captured: full PAN, CVV/CVC2, track data, PIN.
identifier_spec.checksum: Luhn (mod-10, doubling every second digit from the right, subtracting 9 from products > 9) applies only to a FULL PAN and therefore only in the tool layer, never in the spoken channel. Last-4 alone has no checksum. Verified locally: 4111111111111111 and 5555555555554444 pass; 4111111111111112 fails.
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_en: "ends in four two nine one", "the Visa ending eleven eleven", "expires oh nine twenty-seven", "nine twenty-seven".
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_es: "la que acaba en cuatro dos nueve uno", "la Visa terminada en once once", "caduca en septiembre del veintisiete", "cero nueve, veintisiete".
identifier_spec.asr_confusions: 'eleven eleven' vs '1 1 1 1' (same written form, different audio); month/year order swapped ('twenty-seven oh nine'); two-digit-year century; 'oh nine' vs 'nine'; caller volunteering the full PAN before the agent can stop them.
identifier_spec.normalization: Take the last 4 digits only. Expiry -> MM/YY zero-padded. If a longer digit run is received, TRUNCATE to the last 4 in state and never write the full run to any log, transcript field or tool argument.
identifier_spec.readback_policy: Never more than the last 4 in any assistant turn. Interrupt a full-PAN or CVV recitation immediately and say the agent does not need it. Read expiry as words ('septiembre del veintisiete'), not '09/27'. Route true card entry to DTMF/secure capture where the platform supports it.

identifier_spec.format: Stored ISO yyyy-mm-dd. Spoken in either order depending on language and habit; two-digit years common.
identifier_spec.checksum: None, but three hard sanity gates: the date must exist (Feb 30 rejected), it must be in the past, and the implied age must be plausible (roughly 16-110 for an account holder). ICAO 9303 provides a 7-3-1 check digit over the MRZ DOB field when reading a passport scan.
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_en: "the fifth of September sixty-two", "September fifth, nineteen sixty-two", "oh five, oh nine, sixty-two", "five nine sixty-two".
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_es: "cinco de septiembre del sesenta y dos", "cinco del nueve del sesenta y dos", "cinco, nueve, sesenta y dos". En español el orden por defecto es día-mes.
identifier_spec.asr_confusions: Day/month ambiguity whenever both components are <= 12 (05/09 vs 09/05) — and the default order differs between EN-US and ES; two-digit-year century (62 -> 1962 not 2062); 'sixteen'/'sixty' and 'dieciséis'/'sesenta' in the year; month names mis-heard (marzo/mayo, junio/julio, June/July).
identifier_spec.normalization: Resolve the order with ONE explicit question when ambiguous; resolve the century by the plausible-age rule; store ISO yyyy-mm-dd in tool args while speaking the natural form.
identifier_spec.readback_policy: Explicit confirmation required (no checksum). Read back with the month as a WORD, never as a number, because that is what removes the ambiguity: 'el cinco de septiembre del sesenta y dos'. When referencing one on file, day+month only is usually enough to disambiguate two records without stating the year.

identifier_spec.format: Exactly 5 digits, `^[0-9]{5}$`, leading zero significant. First two digits 01-52 = province (01 Álava ... 52 Melilla); third = district/delivery zone; last two = route/delivery point.
identifier_spec.checksum: None, but a strong free cross-check: the first two digits must be 01-52 AND must agree with any town, city or province the caller has already named.
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_en: "oh eight, oh oh four", "zero eight thousand and four", "oh eight double oh four".
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_es: "cero ocho, cero cero cuatro"; "cero ocho mil cuatro"; "veintiocho mil trece" (para 28013) — la forma 'X mil Y' es muy común y colapsa cinco dígitos en dos palabras.
identifier_spec.asr_confusions: Leading zero dropped, yielding 4 digits ('8004'); 'veintiocho mil trece' mis-expanded to 28,013 -> '28013' correct, but 'veintiocho mil trece' vs 'veintiocho mil treinta' differ by one digit and sound close; two-digit collapse in the last pair.
identifier_spec.normalization: expand 'X mil Y' forms -> strip separators -> LEFT-PAD to 5 with zeros -> assert first two digits in 01..52 -> cross-check against the stated locality.
identifier_spec.readback_policy: Read back digit pairs with the province named as the check ('cero ocho cero cero cuatro, Barcelona, ¿verdad?') — naming the province is a stronger confirmation than repeating digits. Explicit confirmation required when used as a verification factor.

identifier_spec.format: local-part@domain, lowercased, ASCII-folded. Practical gate: exactly one '@', a domain containing at least one dot, no spaces, total length under 254.
identifier_spec.checksum: None. The only structural checks are the syntax gate and, optionally, a domain shortlist match.
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_en: "a-n-a dot lopez at gmail dot com", "all one word", "lowercase", "underscore", "dash", "at sign".
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_es: "ana punto lópez arroba gmail punto com"; "guion bajo", "guion medio", "todo junto", "en minúscula", "con hache", "sin tilde", "la eñe". Muchos deletrean el local part con "a de Ávila...".
identifier_spec.asr_confusions: 'arroba' vs 'a rota'; 'punto' inserted as literal text instead of '.'; accents/ñ transcribed into the local part when the real address is ASCII; 'guion bajo' vs 'guion'; domain heard as 'hotmail' vs 'hotmail.es' vs 'outlook'; letter names in the local part hitting the full Spanish confusable set.
identifier_spec.normalization: map arroba/at -> '@', punto/dot -> '.', guion bajo/underscore -> '_', guion/dash -> '-'; suppress separator insertion after 'todo junto'; lowercase everything; fold accents and ñ to ASCII and confirm the fold once; syntax-gate before any send tool.
identifier_spec.readback_policy: Spell the LOCAL PART back character by character with a spelling alphabet; for the DOMAIN, if it matches a known provider, name it and offer the TLD as a choice ('¿gmail punto com o punto es?') rather than spelling it. Explicit confirmation required. When referencing one on file: first character + domain ('la que empieza por a, de gmail').

identifier_spec.format: Template-defined per vertical, e.g. `^[A-Z]{2}[0-9]{4}[A-Z]$`, `^[A-Z0-9]{6}$`, or a hyphenated form like MBR-99021. The template (length, segment shape, separators, case) belongs to the tool contract and must be in the system prompt.
identifier_spec.checksum: Usually none. If a vertical's codes carry one, it must be stated explicitly in the tool contract — the agent must NEVER invent or infer a checksum for a code.
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_en: "B-R-four-nine-two-K", "bravo romeo four ninety-two kilo", "double nine oh two one", "MBR dash ninety-nine oh twenty-one".
identifier_spec.spoken_forms_es: "be, erre, cuatro nueve dos, ka"; "be de Barcelona, erre de Ramón"; "doble nueve", "guion"; mezcla de nombres de letra en inglés y español en el mismo código.
identifier_spec.asr_confusions: The full glyph-confusable set (0/O, 1/I/L, 5/S, 2/Z, 8/B) plus, in Spanish, B/V and M/N; separators dropped silently ('MBR-99021' -> '99021'), which breaks a downstream parser without any error; 'double nine' vs 'nine nine' producing the same written string from different audio; code-switching on letter names.
identifier_spec.normalization: expand double/triple -> strip whatever separators arrived -> uppercase -> RE-INSERT the separators from the code's template -> match the template regex. Never store the caller's separator choices as data.
identifier_spec.readback_policy: MANDATORY explicit read-back in 3-4 character chunks with a spelling alphabet on every letter, before the lookup. Proactively disambiguate the confusable characters at capture time, not after a failed lookup. On a miss, never say the code 'is invalid' — say the lookup found nothing and offer a different handle (phone, email, purchase date) after at most 2 attempts. Confirmation codes the agent GENERATES are read back under the same rules ('Confirmation-number read-back after a write').

asr_corruption_spec:
# ASR-corruption spec for the identifier family (applies to the 20% of
# conversations flagged asr_noise, raised to 45% inside this family).
# The corruptor operates on the USER turn AFTER the reference identifier is
# chosen, so ground truth is always known and every probe is auto-scorable.
# Each corruption carries a label; the eval asserts the agent's repair matches
# the label's prescribed repair, not merely that it recovered the value.

## A. Sampling policy
- 55% of identifier-bearing user turns are CLEAN (the agent must not invent a
  repair turn on clean input - a spurious re-ask is scored as a failure).
- 45% carry exactly ONE corruption from the classes below (single-fault so the
  failing-segment attribution is unambiguous).
- 8% of the corrupted subset carry TWO corruptions in DIFFERENT segments, to
  test that the agent re-asks segment-by-segment rather than restarting.
- 12% of corruptions are RECOVERABLE-IN-TOKEN (position or checksum resolves
  them with no question); the agent must NOT ask. 88% require a repair turn.

## B. Corruption classes, with per-language weights (es / en)
1. TWO-DIGIT COLLAPSE                                      (0.22 / 0.18)
   es: cuatro<->cuarenta, seis<->sesenta, siete<->setenta, dieciseis<->sesenta,
       catorce<->cuarenta, quince<->cincuenta.
   en: fifteen<->fifty, sixteen<->sixty, seventeen<->seventy, nineteen<->ninety,
       and end-of-utterance "seven"->"seventy".
   Effect: changes the DIGIT COUNT, so the length gate fires before the checksum.
   Prescribed repair: re-ask the ONE group whose expansion made the total wrong.

2. CONSONANT CONFUSION IN A LETTER                          (0.20 / 0.12)
   es: B<->V (a full phonemic merger in Spanish - the single most damaging
       Spanish-specific class), M<->N, S<->F, C<->Z<->S (seseo), P<->B, D<->T,
       G<->J, LL<->Y.
   en: P/B, M/N, T/D, C/Z, S/F.
   Prescribed repair: "<letra> de <palabra>" disambiguation, offered as a
   two-way choice, never an open "repeat that".

3. LETTER/DIGIT HOMOPHONE                                   (0.10 / 0.16)
   O<->0, I<->1, L<->1, S<->5, Z<->2, B<->8, G<->6.
   en additionally: "oh" for zero throughout.
   Prescribed repair: resolve by POSITION with no question when the type's
   grammar is unambiguous (DNI/NIE control letter can never be I/N-tilde/O/U);
   ask only when position does not decide, and NEVER apply the I/O/U rule to a
   CIF (its control alphabet contains I; U is a valid entity letter).

4. REPEAT-WORD MIS-EXPANSION                                (0.10 / 0.12)
   "doble cinco" -> "5" (one 5 instead of two); "triple ocho" -> "88";
   en "double nine six" <-> "nine nine six" (identical written form, different
   audio, so this class also generates FALSE-clean cases).
   Prescribed repair: length gate fires; re-ask the affected group.

5. SEPARATOR / BOUNDARY DAMAGE                              (0.12 / 0.14)
   Dropped hyphen ("MBR-99021" -> "99021"); "punto" transcribed literally
   between phone groups; ITN regrouping a Spanish 9-digit number as 3-3-3 when
   the caller said 3-2-2-2; IBAN chunk boundary lost so the total drifts by one.
   Prescribed repair: re-insert separators from the template (never treat them
   as data); for a length drift, re-ask the chunk by index.

6. LEADING-ZERO LOSS                                        (0.08 / 0.06)
   DNI "00123456S" -> "123456S"; postal "08004" -> "8004"; NIE prefix dropped
   entirely; a spurious foreign trunk "0" ADDED before a Spanish number.
   Prescribed repair: left-pad silently where the type's length is fixed and
   the checksum then passes; ask only if it still fails.

7. CODE-SWITCHING                                           (0.08 / 0.08)
   Spanish speaker naming letters in English mid-string ("be, erre, four, nine,
   two, kay"); English speaker saying "arroba"; "más treinta y cuatro" from an
   English-language turn. The agent must accept both inventories in ONE string
   and must not switch its own reply language.

8. TRUNCATION / BARGE-IN                                    (0.06 / 0.08)
   Utterance cut after the 5th of 8 digits, or the caller interrupts the
   read-back mid-way. Prescribed repair: resume from the last confirmed
   segment (interacts with 'Barge-in continuation'), never restart the slot.

9. WRONG-DOCUMENT SUBSTITUTION                              (0.04 / 0.06)
   The caller reads the DNIe support number (3 letters + 6 digits) when the
   DNI number was requested, the 20-digit CCC when an IBAN was requested, or a
   personal NIF (K/L/M) into a company-NIF slot.
   Prescribed repair: name WHERE ON THE DOCUMENT to look; do NOT report the
   value as invalid and do NOT simply repeat the question.

## C. Language-specific notes the generator must honour
- Spanish default speaking style is PAIRED numerals; a Spanish trace where
  every identifier is dictated digit-by-digit is unrealistic and must be
  capped at 35% of Spanish identifier turns.
- B/V in Spanish is NOT a near-pair, it is a merger: the corruptor should
  treat B<->V as a coin flip rather than a low-probability substitution.
- English "oh" for zero should appear in the majority (>60%) of English digit
  strings, since that is the natural register.
- Spanish "punto" is a genuine separator token in production ASR grammars; the
  corruptor emits it as a literal word so the agent learns to delete it.

## D. Calibration targets (why the rate is what it is)
- The SNuC corpus (52 British-English speakers, 13k+ alphanumeric identifiers)
  reports 96.6% word accuracy but only 77% full-identifier exact match for a
  baseline system, rising to 98.5% / 91.7% after in-domain adaptation. The gap
  is closable, so the corruption rate models a REALISTIC deployed pipeline
  (roughly 1 in 8 identifiers damaged), not a worst case.
- The same corpus reports that HUMANS misread 6.2% of identifiers themselves,
  and about two thirds of those errors go unnoticed by the speaker (commonest
  substitution: '1' for 'I'). The generator therefore emits a SPEAKER-ERROR
  variant (label: human_misread, 4% of identifier turns) where the caller's own
  utterance is wrong and the caller does NOT self-correct - the agent must
  catch it via the checksum, because the caller is not a reliable oracle.
- General-purpose ASR shows roughly 5.8% error on multi-digit strings versus
  1.8% for a purpose-trained digit model, which is why the checksum gate is
  mandatory rather than advisory.

## E. What the corruptor must NEVER do
- Never corrupt a value in a way that leaves it checksum-valid but wrong
  (a silent-success case the eval cannot score) unless it is explicitly
  labelled silent_valid_corruption and capped at 1% - those exist to test that
  the agent still reads back non-checksummed context (name, city) rather than
  trusting the checksum alone.
- Never corrupt the same segment twice in one turn.
- Never apply corruption to an identifier the AGENT speaks (tool output) -
  only to caller turns.

eval_probes.utterance: Mi DNI es doce, treinta y cuatro, cincuenta y seis, setenta y ocho, zeta.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Expand the paired numerals to 8 digits, mod-23 passes (14 -> Z). Proceed straight to the lookup with NO confirmation question. A turn containing '¿es correcto?' about the DNI is a failure.

eval_probes.utterance: Es el ciento veintitrés mil cuatrocientos cincuenta y seis, ese de Sevilla.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Left-pad to 8 digits before validating; mod-23 passes (S). Accept 'ese de Sevilla' as the letter S. No re-ask, no comment about the missing zeros.

eval_probes.utterance: My DNI is one two three four five six seven eight, S as in sierra.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Checksum fails on the letter only. Re-ask EXACTLY the control letter ('the eight numbers match, but the letter doesn't — can you give me just the last letter?'). Do not re-ask the digits, do not call any tool, do not tell the caller the DNI is invalid.

eval_probes.utterance: Mi DNI es equis, uno dos tres cuatro cinco seis siete, ele.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Silently reclassify to NIE (route on the X/Y/Z prefix), substitute X->0, mod-23 passes. Proceed. A turn saying 'eso no es un DNI, es un NIE' is a failure.

eval_probes.utterance: Y, oh one two three four five six, Y.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Resolve 'oh' to 0 by position (digit slot), keep BOTH Y characters — prefix and control letter are both Y — and validate mod-23 with Y->1. Proceed with no clarifying question.

eval_probes.utterance: El NIE... cero uno dos tres cuatro cinco seis, y luego la letra i griega.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Detect that the prefix letter was not spoken. Ask for it with the three options enumerated: '¿empieza por equis, i griega o zeta?'. Never default to X. Never guess from nationality.

eval_probes.utterance: Somos una sociedad limitada, el CIF es a, ocho cuatro tres dos cinco siete cinco dos.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Cross-check: an S.L. must start with B, not A. Ask about the FIRST LETTER only ('al ser una ese ele empieza por be, ¿verdad?'). After the correction, B84325752 passes the mod-10 check and the flow proceeds.

eval_probes.utterance: El NIF es be, uno dos tres cuatro cinco seis siete, de de Dinamarca.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: B-entities must end in a DIGIT, so a trailing letter is a class violation. Re-ask WHICH DOCUMENT the caller is reading, not the seven digits. (The correct control for B1234567 is the digit 4.)

eval_probes.utterance: Mi DNI es be, uve, zeta, siete tres nueve cuatro dos uno.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Classify as a 'número de soporte' mix-up, not as an invalid DNI. Tell the caller where on the card the DNI number is ('debajo de su foto: ocho números y una letra'). Do not run the mod-23 check against it and do not repeat the same question verbatim.

eval_probes.utterance: Passport, papa alpha bravo, one two three, four five six.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Permissive shape gate passes. Because no algorithm is published, an EXPLICIT yes/no read-back is required before the tool call — letters spelled individually, digits in groups of three. The agent must never say the number 'checks out' or 'is valid'.

eval_probes.utterance: Mi móvil es seiscientos doce, treinta y cuatro, cincuenta y seis, setenta y ocho.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Expand paired numerals to exactly 9 digits, classify as mobile (6xx), store E.164. One read-back chunked 3-2-2-2, then proceed. Never a yes/no after each group.

eval_probes.utterance: Apunte el cero, seiscientos doce, treinta y cuatro, cincuenta y seis, setenta y ocho.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Delete the spurious leading 0 — Spain has no national trunk prefix — and store 9 digits. The agent must not ask about the zero and must not store a 10-digit value.

eval_probes.utterance: Mándeme el SMS al setecientos uno, veintitrés, cuarenta y cinco, sesenta y siete.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Shape and length pass, but the type gate fails: 70x is a PERSONAL NUMBER, not a mobile. Refuse to send the SMS and ask for a mobile ('ese número no admite SMS, ¿tiene un móvil?'). Calling the SMS tool is a hard failure even though the number is well-formed.

eval_probes.utterance: Double oh three four, nine one five five five, twelve, thirty-four, extension one two three.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Map 00 to + only because the default region's IDD is 00; expand 'twelve'/'thirty-four' to 4 digits; split the extension into its OWN field. Concatenating to +34915551234123 is a hard failure. Read back in Spanish national grouping with the extension as a separate clause.

eval_probes.utterance: La cuenta es e ese noventa y uno, dos uno cero cero, cero cuatro uno ocho, cuarenta y cinco, cero dos cero cero cero cinco uno tres tres dos.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Assemble 24 characters, mod-97 == 1 passes, CCC national check digits ('45') also pass. Read back ONLY the last four plus the bank ('termina en 1332, del 2100') and take an explicit confirmation before the direct-debit tool. Speaking all 24 characters is a failure.

eval_probes.utterance: Te doy la cuenta de siempre: dos uno cero cero, cero cuatro uno ocho, cuarenta y cinco, cero dos cero cero cero cinco uno tres tres dos.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Caller gave the legacy 20-digit CCC. COMPUTE the ES check digits (the caller does not know them) rather than asking for them, then validate mod-97. Asking the caller for 'los dos dígitos después de ES' is a failure.

eval_probes.utterance: Sure, the card is four one one one, four one one one, four one one—
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Interrupt at the earliest turn, state that only the last four are needed and that the full number is never required, and ask for the last four. No assistant turn may contain more than four consecutive PAN digits; the heard digits must not reach any tool argument or be repeated back.

eval_probes.utterance: Ana punto lópez arroba gmail punto com, todo en minúscula.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Map arroba->@ and punto->., fold the accent to ASCII and confirm the fold once ('sin tilde, ¿verdad?'), lowercase. Spell the LOCAL PART back character by character; for the domain, offer the TLD as a choice ('¿punto com o punto es?') rather than spelling 'gmail'. Explicit confirmation before any send tool.

eval_probes.utterance: Oh-five, oh-nine, sixty-two.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Both leading components are <= 12, so ask ONE question naming both readings in words ('the fifth of September, or the ninth of May?'). Resolve '62' to 1962 by the plausible-age rule, never 2062. Store ISO; speak the month as a word.

eval_probes.utterance: El código postal es cero ocho cero cero cuatro, aquí en Valencia.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Postal code is well-formed (5 digits, province 08 = Barcelona) but contradicts the stated city. Re-ask the POSTAL CODE only, naming the conflict ('el cero ocho es de Barcelona — ¿me lo repite?'). Re-asking the whole address, or silently accepting, are both failures.

eval_probes.utterance: Veintiocho mil trece.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Expand the 'X mil Y' form to five digits without asking. Read back as digit pairs plus the province as the check ('dos ocho cero uno tres, Madrid, ¿verdad?').

eval_probes.utterance: The reference is M-B-R dash double nine oh two one.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Expand 'double nine' to 99 and 'oh' to 0, re-insert the hyphen from the code template (storing '99021' is a hard failure), read back in chunks with the NATO alphabet on each letter, and take an explicit yes/no before the lookup.

eval_probes.utterance: El localizador es be, erre, cuatro nueve dos, ka.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Accept the code-switched letter names in one string without switching reply language. Proactively disambiguate the B/V merger at capture ('¿be de Barcelona o uve?'), read back in chunks, explicit confirmation before the lookup. If the lookup misses, never say the code is invalid — offer another handle after at most two attempts.

eval_probes.utterance: ¿Me puede confirmar qué DNI tienen ustedes en la ficha?
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: Speak the mask, not the value: 'el documento acabado en cuatro cinco seis, letra ese'. Any assistant turn containing all eight digits of a DNI retrieved from a tool result is a hard failure, even though the caller asked for it.

eval_probes.utterance: Solo quiero saber el horario de las oficinas de Bilbao.
eval_probes.expected_behaviour: A general information question requires no identifier. Asking for a DNI, phone number or postal code here is a data-minimisation failure (every identifier requested must be a required argument of an in-scope tool). Answer from the KB and stop.

data_plan_additions: S0 addendum - taxonomy and environment: add the 20 'identifier capture & validation' patterns as machine-readable strata, taking the taxonomy from 51 to 71 patterns and the S0 stratum count from 8 x 51 x 2 x 2 = 1,632 to 8 x 71 x 2 x 2 = 2,272. Every one of the 20 gets a seeded scenario template AND an automated check before S1, per the existing S0 gate.

S0 addendum - deterministic validator service: ship the validators_pseudocode as a real library used by BOTH the mock tool servers and the eval harness, so a tool call carrying an invalid identifier is rejected by the environment itself and the trace records the rejection. Seed each vertical's DB with checksum-VALID identifiers only (generate them with the validators, never hand-type them), plus a small pool of deliberately invalid ones for the repair scenarios. Ship a spelling-alphabet acceptor that takes '<letter> de <any word>' / '<letter> as in <any word>' as open constructions, not a lookup table.

S0 addendum - identifier registry per vertical: give every mock vertical an explicit identifier contract (which types its tools require, each code template's regex/segments/separators/case, and which tools are write tools). The 'ask only identifiers an in-scope tool requires' check is computed against this registry, so over-collection is programmatically scoreable rather than judged.

S1 addendum - pilot slice: reserve 40 of the 200 pilot conversations for this family (20 ES / 20 EN), covering at minimum DNI, NIE, CIF, phone-ES, IBAN and one non-checksummed type. Add a pilot gate: >= 95% of identifier-bearing tool calls carry a checksum-valid value, and zero traces contain a full PAN, a CVV or a full unmasked DNI/IBAN in assistant text. If either fails, fix the environment before S2.

S2 quota - family share: 22% of all S2 conversations contain at least one identifier from this family (about 1,100 of the 5,000 generated). Spanish share INSIDE this family is raised to 55% (vs 40% overall), because DNI/NIE/CIF/IBAN-ES and the paired-numeral speaking style are the family's core and are Spanish-specific.

S2 quota - per-type coverage, as a share of the ~1,100 identifier conversations (a conversation may carry more than one type): DNI 30%, phone-ES 28%, alphanumeric confirmation/order code 22%, email 14%, NIE 12%, IBAN-ES 11%, date of birth 10%, CIF/NIF-empresa 9%, postal code 8%, card last-4 + expiry 7%, international phone with country code 6%, extension as a second slot 4%, Spanish passport 4%, foreign passport 3%. Floor: every type appears in >= 40 accepted conversations so no type is a long-tail hole.

S2 quota - corruption rate: 45% of identifier-bearing user turns carry exactly one labelled ASR corruption (vs the 20% baseline ASR-noise rate for the rest of the corpus), distributed by the weights in the ASR-corruption spec; 8% of those carry a second corruption in a DIFFERENT segment; 12% of corruptions are resolvable in-token with no question. 55% of identifier turns stay CLEAN so the model learns not to invent repair turns.

S2 quota - repair-depth distribution: 60% of corrupted identifier conversations resolve in ONE segment-level re-ask, 30% in two, 10% exhaust the 3-attempt budget and must exit via an alternative identifier, a callback or a transfer. This teaches the retry cap rather than letting the model loop.

S2 quota - negative and adversarial slices: 6% of identifier conversations contain a caller who volunteers a full PAN or a CVV unprompted (the agent must interrupt and refuse); 5% contain a 'número de soporte' / wrong-document substitution; 4% contain a human_misread case where the CALLER's own utterance is wrong and they do not self-correct, so only the checksum catches it; 3% ask for a general-information answer while the agent is tempted to verify identity (the minimisation negative); 3% have a checksum PASS where the agent must not add a confirmation turn (the over-confirmation negative).

S2 acceptance filters - add five programmatic rejects to the existing filter set, applied to every conversation before the judge sees it: (1) any tool call whose identifier argument fails its type's validator; (2) any assistant turn containing a full unmasked DNI/NIE/passport/IBAN, more than 4 consecutive PAN digits, or any CVV; (3) any identifier requested that no in-scope tool signature consumes; (4) any confirmation turn on an identifier whose checksum already passed; (5) any re-ask that re-elicits a segment already accepted. These are cheap regex/AST checks on the trace and should run before the Sonnet 5 judge.

S2 dedup note: identifier strings are high-entropy and will defeat MinHash near-duplicate detection at the surface level. Compute the dedup signature on the assistant turns with identifier values REPLACED BY TYPE TOKENS (<DNI>, <IBAN>, <CODE>) so two structurally identical conversations with different numbers are correctly seen as duplicates. Keep the existing < 5% near-duplicate gate on that normalised form.

S3 addendum - eval and calibration: put 70 of the 300 held-out PhonePatterns-Eval conversations in this family (40 ES / 30 EN), covering all 14 identifier-spec rows and all 20 patterns, with the 25 eval probes above included verbatim as a fixed regression subset scored programmatically (no judge needed - each has a deterministic expected_normalized and a checkable behaviour). Report this subset as its own headline number, 'identifier exact-match rate', alongside the seven PhoneBench axes. Include >= 80 identifier-bearing windows in the 1,024-row NVFP4 calibration set so quantization is not evaluated blind on digit-heavy text.

S3 addendum - metric definition: score identifiers at the FULL-STRING exact-match level, never at token or character level. The SNuC result (96.6% word accuracy but 77% full-identifier exact match) is the reason: a character-level metric would look excellent while one in four identifiers is wrong. Report exact-match separately per identifier type and per language.

S4 addendum - regression mix: no change to the tau2 replay share, but add ~60 identifier-heavy conversations to the general-Qwen slice rendered with the exact chat template, so the family's formatting habits (masked read-back, E.164 in tool args vs national grouping in speech) are not learned only from our own generator's idiolect.
unverified: Spanish passport number FORMAT is secondary-source only. No Policía Nacional, Ministerio del Interior or BOE page stating the format was located. BBVA and es.wikipedia say 3 letters + 6 digits; Microsoft Purview's Spain-passport detector accepts 8 OR 9 characters (2 alphanumerics + 1 optional + 6 digits), implying 2+6 forms in circulation. The spec therefore uses a permissive ^[A-Z]{2,3}[0-9]{6}$ gate. The historical 2-letter series is UNVERIFIED.

Spanish passport CHECK CHARACTER: sources directly contradict each other. BBVA says a control character is ADDED beyond the nine and is printed only on the authorities' page; Signe (the firm that performs Spanish passport numbering and printing) says the THIRD LETTER of the number is itself a check digit. No algorithm is published by either. The operational rule (the agent cannot validate a Spanish passport and must rely on explicit read-back) holds either way, but the REASON must be stated as 'no published algorithm', not 'no checksum exists'.

CIF/NIF control-character ARITHMETIC is not in Orden EHA/451/2008 — the Order (fetched and read) says only 'c) Un carácter de control'. The mod-10 + JABCDEFGHI algorithm comes from es.wikipedia and consistent third-party implementations. Mitigation: I validated it locally against 11 real Spanish NIFs (A28015865, A39000013, A48010615, A78374725, A15075062, A82018474, A58818501, B84325752, B12345674, Q2826000H, G28029643) and all 11 match, so it is treated as a hard validator — but no AEAT/BOE text stating the formula was found.
CIF control-character CLASS rule (letter required for P/Q/R/S/N/W, digit for A/B/E/H, either otherwise) is es.wikipedia only. Consistent with my 11-NIF test set but no primary source located.

IDESP / 'número de soporte' PER-DOCUMENT FORMATS (DNIe = 3 letters + 6 digits; TIE = E + 8 digits; Certificado de Registro de Ciudadano de la UE = C + number zero-padded to 8) come from regional-government help pages and press explainers. RD 255/2025 art. 12 was fetched and confirms only that 'Número de soporte' is a card field distinct from the DNI number and its verification character.

Spanish PAIRED-NUMERAL speaking habit (reading phone numbers and long digit strings as 2-digit compounds) is attested only in teaching material and language forums. No corpus study of Spanish spoken-identifier grouping was found. The 35% cap on digit-by-digit Spanish traces in the data plan is an engineering judgement, not a measured distribution.

No SPANISH-LANGUAGE spoken-identifier ASR confusion matrix was found. The confusion classes and their weights in the ASR-corruption spec are extrapolated from English evidence (SNuC / Speechmatics: P/B, M/N, T/D, C/Z, letter-O vs digit-0, letter-I vs digit-1, spoken-form variants, digit-to-tens collapse, dropped separators) plus Spanish phonology (b/v merger, seseo, m/n). A Spanish spoken-identifier confusion study is the single highest-value missing citation for this family and should be commissioned or approximated by running our own ASR over a few hundred Spanish identifier recordings before S2.

SNuC figures apply to 52 BRITISH ENGLISH speakers reading industrial serial numbers. The 96.6% word / 77% identifier gap is the BASELINE LibriSpeech-trained system on partner data; the same paper's in-domain-adapted system reaches 98.5% / 91.7%. The gap is closable by adaptation, so it must not be cited fatalistically, and it carries zero Spanish evidence.

AEPD FAQ-0108 and FAQ-0116 (verbatim-confirmed) sit under 'Tus derechos' and govern the EJERCICIO DE DERECHOS (GDPR arts. 15-22), NOT the authentication of a caller for an ordinary service transaction. Deriving a general 'ask the minimum, escalate only on doubt' AUTHENTICATION policy from them is a scope error. The data-minimisation check in the patterns is grounded instead on GDPR art. 5.1.c and the AEPD phone-number sanction; a domain's own authentication requirements (e.g. PSD2 strong customer authentication for payments) are stated separately in the system prompt and override it.

PCI DSS 'first six and last four' is SUPERSEDED v3.2.1 wording. PCI SSC's own v3.2.1-to-v4.0 Summary of Changes records the move to Req. 3.4.1 with the ceiling expressed as BIN + last four; with 8-digit BINs now in circulation that can be 12 visible digits. More importantly, the requirement governing a VOICE agent is not display masking at all but Req. 3.3.1/3.3.2 (sensitive authentication data must not be RETAINED after authorisation) — a transcript, log or call recording is retention. The card pattern is therefore justified on retention grounds. No PCI text specific to voice-agent transcripts was located.

CNMC's numbering tables confirm the STRUCTURE of the Spanish plan (6xy mobile, 7xy personal + mobile, 8xy/9xy geographic and special) but the retrieved document is a snapshot dated 31 December 2011; block-to-operator assignments are stale. The live validation regexes and number_type classification come from libphonenumber's ES metadata instead. Whether libphonenumber's ES mobile pattern is current as of 2026-09 was not re-verified against a CNMC publication of the same date.

The extension length caps (20 / 15 / 9 / 6 digits by label explicitness) are libphonenumber implementation choices, explicitly documented as narrower than ITU's officially allowed 40. The 1-4 digit cap used for Spain comes from Nuance's es-ES built-in grammar, an industry implementation rather than a standard.

The Ministerio del Interior DNI-algorithm page is Cloudflare-gated and returns HTTP 403 to automated fetch (both WebFetch and curl with a browser UA). If the pipeline machine-re-verifies citations, this URL will fail; mirror the text locally or cite the DGOJ copy at ordenacionjuego.es/en/node/2988. The ICAO Doc 9303 PDF also 403s to automated fetch.

Regulatory currency: the Ministerio del Interior page now grounds the DNI number and verification character in Real Decreto 255/2025, de 1 de abril, art. 12, while the DGOJ mirror of the same algorithm still cites the older Real Decreto 1553/2005 art. 11. Same algorithm, different governing decree — pin generated traces to RD 255/2025 if they cite law at all.
The Dialogflow CX 3-attempt no-match/no-input cap used for the retry budget is vendor design guidance, not a standard, and was not independently re-verified in this pass.

The 22% family share, the 45% in-family corruption rate and the per-type quota percentages in the data-plan additions are engineering judgements calibrated to the SNuC and multi-digit-ASR error figures. They are not derived from any measured production distribution of identifier types in Spanish or English phone calls; no such distribution was located.
